verdict.rationale: Temporal documents first-party versioning of automations: Worker Versioning tags Workers and rolls them out as versioned deployments, and Workflow versioning applies code changes to new executions while in-progress ones keep the original code. A community user adds that after deploying new code you can reset an execution to an earlier point and re-run it, but rolling back a deployment to a prior version and any review or approval step are not documented by the product; reviewing workflows-as-code in git would be a user-side workaround. Missing for 10: a documented review/approval workflow for automation changes, explicit first-party rollback of a deployment to a previous version, first-party docs for execution reset, and independent hands-on corroboration of versioning.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: The Worker Versioning feature allows you to tag your Workers and programmatically roll them out in versioned deployments, so that old Workers can run old code paths and new Workers can run new code paths.
you can modify your Workflow Definition so that new executions use the updated code, while existing ones continue running the original version
After you deploy new workflow code, you can reset a workflow's execution state to before a given statement was called, and it will re-run from there.
